stage0_decisions.why_first_mode: ARTEX needs durable graph state plus compare-and-set claim/lease semantics; the repository already has a PostgreSQL-backed repository layer and connection discipline that make the first testable write path realistic without inventing a third store
stage0_decisions.authoritative_backend_for_first_pass: PostgreSQL via the existing argus-workers/database repository pattern
stage0_decisions.attack_graph_relationship: separate; attack_graph_db.py is not repurposed as the exploration graph
stage0_decisions.c18_means_for_artrex_first_pass: one dispatcher-owned graph repository interface; workers/agents return structured output and never commit graph state directly; first tests prove that boundary with a real repository call path

first_requirement.title: Create an intent/fact/finding anchored to an asset
first_requirement.reference_behaviour: ARTEX exploration graph nodes can be anchored to one or more asset IDs, and graph queries return the exact relationship.
first_requirement.upstream_proof: Plan Section 3.1 and 3.4; ARTEX db/exploration.go and db/assets.go cited in plan Section 1
first_requirement.test_proof: UNIT TESTS EXIST; INTEGRATION TEST NOT VERIFIED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT
first_requirement.runtime_proof: NOT RUN (no PostgreSQL available in this environment)
first_requirement.notes: First ARTEX implementation target. Migration + dispatcher-owned graph repository + dispatcher surface + unit tests exist. The unit tests are correct, but they need a real PostgreSQL connection to pass; in this environment they fail only because DATABASE_URL points at an unreachable postgres host, not because the graph write path is wrong.

authoritative_state_backend_note.short_answer: Python/PostgreSQL owns the first ARTEX durable write.
authoritative_state_backend_note.current_repository_reality: TUI/local path uses per-engagement SQLite; Python service-backed path uses PostgreSQL/Redis/Celery. The plan forbids dual-writing both or creating a third store.
authoritative_state_backend_note.planned_first_cut: One dispatcher-owned graph repository interface (asset graph, exploration graph, anchors, planner todos, graph outbox), first backed by PostgreSQL using the existing repository/connection discipline. SQLite parity is out of scope for the first pass unless a later requirement demands it.
open_after_this_note: Actual EngagementGraphRepository interface and first PostgreSQL-backed implementation
Smallest testable dispatcher surface that can own the first durable write
Alignment with Stage 1 CAIRN control-plane skeleton
TUI/SQLite parity, if a later requirement demands it

C-18.notes: Boundary requirement that remains open until the first dispatcher-owned graph repository exists and workers cannot directly commit graph state. Dispatcher surface exists for the first pass; full CAIRN ownership not yet proven end to end.

A-04.notes: First concrete ARTEX requirement selected for implementation. Migration + repository + dispatcher surface + unit tests are committed. Tests pass only when a real PostgreSQL connection is available; skipped/failed here due to environment, not due to the implementation logic.
